node_names: Year 12 / Research Methodology / Research process / conducting research
Year 12 / Research Methodology / Research process / planning for research

content.text: Harry is conducting an independent research project on student participation in organised sport during the Higher School Certificate year. Harry will need to conduct research using a range of research methods. Explain the steps involved in conducting this research, supporting each step with relevant examples.

Sample answer: Access sources of data (secondary data and literature review, then primary data such as questionnaires and interviews); collect and record data; document actions and issues; interpret findings and form conclusions.

items: 6 marks: demonstrates extensive knowledge and understanding of each step involved when conducting research about participation in organised sport during the HSC year; provides a clear link between the components of the research process; provides relevant examples for all steps conducted.

5 marks: demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding of each step involved when conducting research; provides a link between the components of the research process; provides relevant example(s) for all steps conducted.

4 marks: demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of the steps involved when conducting research; attempts to link components of the research process; provides relevant example(s) for the step(s).
2-3 marks: provides some information about the step(s) involved when conducting research.

node_names: Year 12 / Parenting and Caring / Parenting / authoritarian
Year 12 / Parenting and Caring / Parenting / outline the roles of parents and carers and evaluate the significance of each role in various parenting and caring situations

content.text: Joseph and Sarah have chosen an authoritarian parenting style for their 3-year-old son and 16-year-old daughter.
What are the characteristics of an authoritarian parenting style?
Sample answer: Authoritarian parenting styles are rigid, inflexible and do not allow dependants to contribute to decision making; they enforce strict rules and consequences.

items: 2 marks: provides characteristics of an authoritarian style of parenting.

content.text: What are the effects an authoritarian parenting style could have on this family?

Sample answer: Authoritarian parenting is inflexible with preconceived goals; it promotes clear boundaries and communication but may limit the child's independence and create fear, especially for the 3-year-old and 16-year-old.

items: 4 marks: demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding of the effects an authoritarian parenting style could have on this family; provides clear points for and/or against; provides relevant examples.
3 marks: demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of the effects; provides point(s) for and/or against; provides relevant example(s).
2 marks: provides some information about the effects of an authoritarian parenting style.
2 marks: part (a) identifies characteristics of an authoritarian parenting style.
4 marks: part (b) explains effects of an authoritarian parenting style on this family.

node_names: Year 12 / Parenting and Caring / Parenting / carers
Year 12 / Parenting and Caring / Parenting / Support for parents and carers

content.text: Sally cares for both her teenage son and her elderly mother who has a physical disability. Compare the strategies Sally would use in her roles as a parent and a carer, using relevant examples.

Sample answer: Similarities include satisfying specific needs (food, shelter, economic support) and building positive relationships; differences include home modifications and wheelchair access for the mother and educational support for the son.

items: 8 marks: demonstrates extensive knowledge and understanding about parenting and caring roles; provides extensive information on how the strategies used are similar and/or different for the roles; provides relevant examples.

6-7 marks: demonstrates thorough knowledge and understanding about parenting and caring roles; provides thorough information on how the strategies used are similar and/or different; provides relevant examples.

4-5 marks: demonstrates sound knowledge about parenting and caring roles; provides information about strategies that can be used for both parent and carer; attempts to show similarity and/or difference; provides example(s).
2-3 marks: provides some information about parenting and/or caring and/or strategies.
1 mark: provides a relevant point about parenting or caring or a strategy.
